# Promoted to repo memory: commit-attribution

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `commit-attribution M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-13T08:02:19.961Z) — `sofar new <slug>` binds the current branch by default, silently replacing whatever binding that branch already had. On a repo like this one — where main carries a live initiative and several sessions share the worktree — that knocks the in-flight initiative off the branch peer sessions and hooks resolve through, with no warning. Check `.sofar/bindings.json` before running it; pass `--no-bind` when the current branch is already bound to live work, then reach the new record with `sofar switch <slug>` or a dedicated branch.
- **M2** (2026-08-13T08:12:05.394Z) — Trailer probe results, git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155), run 2026-08-13 before D4 was taken. Read incantation: `git log --format='%h|%(trailers:key=Sofar-Initiative,valueonly,separator=%x2C)'`. Always pass `separator=` — bare `valueonly` emits a TRAILING NEWLINE that corrupts any line-oriented parse.

Survival: cherry-pick PRESERVES the trailer; rebase PRESERVES it (rebase is a cherry-pick sequence); a commit with no trailer reads back as an empty field, never as a guess.

KNOWN LOSSY PATH — squash merge. `git merge --squash` writes SQUASH_MSG with each original message INDENTED BY FOUR SPACES, so git's trailer parser does not see it and the squashed commit reads back as empty. Committing with `-m` discards SQUASH_MSG entirely and loses it the same way. The slug text is still present verbatim in the body, so a fallback that scans the body for an indented marker recovers it exactly — still reading git, not guessing. Consequence if unhandled: a squash-merged initiative reads as "not shipped" when it did ship — a FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the safe direction but still wrong. Not an issue while this repo commits straight to main; it becomes one the first time work lands through a squashed PR.
- **M3** (2026-08-13T08:19:56.315Z) — Claude Code exports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID into the agent's shell, and its value is EXACTLY the session id sofar registers (verified 2026-08-13 against a live session: env value matched the injected "Session: <id>" line character for character). Critically, git hooks INHERIT it — a probe prepare-commit-msg hook wrote the live session id into a commit message. That is what makes automatic, exact commit attribution possible from a process that has no access to the MCP server's in-memory pin: resolve the env var through homeInitiative (mcp/context.ts:174, already imported by cli/event.ts) rather than through bindings.json.

Related vars present in the same environment: CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION.

CAVEAT: none of these are a documented contract — they are Claude Code implementation details and can disappear in any release. Anything depending on them must degrade to silence, never to a branch-binding guess (D5's standing rule), and the silence must be visible or the signal rots without anyone noticing.
- **M4** (2026-08-13T08:38:21.531Z) — VERSION SKEW makes commit attribution a silent no-op, and nothing currently reports it. The prepare-commit-msg shim guards with `command -v sofar`, which succeeds for ANY installed sofar — including one too old to have the `commit-trailer` subcommand. The unknown subcommand then fails, `|| true` swallows it, and the hook exits 0. Result: the hook is installed, every commit looks normal, and nothing is ever attributed.

Confirmed live on 2026-08-13: the sofar on PATH here is 0.25.1, which predates `commit-trailer`, so installing the hook in this repo TODAY would attribute nothing until a release carrying the command is published and installed. Verified by running `sofar commit-trailer --help` against the global binary — it fell through to top-level help rather than the subcommand.

This is the concrete form of the exposure task 2.5(b) names: silence is the correct behaviour per D5, but invisible silence rots. The safety net is 2.4's doctor check (commits on the branch carrying no trailer), which is NOT built yet. Until it is, assume attribution is off unless a commit has been verified to carry the trailer.
